messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — sudden spike: 18x baseline requests to /v1/embeddings from multiple IP clusters, 40% failure rate, CPU on inference fleet rising. Auto-escalate to oncall.
ivy-oncall: on it. seeing big fanout from three ASN ranges, lots of small requests, likely scraping.
ben-sre: can you dump top client keys and user agents? also check KV cache hit ratio, might be bypassing prefix cache.
ivy-oncall: pasted small sample in #eng-runtime: `curl sample-key: 30k reqs/min, UA: python-requests/2.*`
nina-support: any active customer reports? CX only seeing increased latency page on status for a handful of customers.
liz-sec: suggests credential-spray + scraper. recommend enabling WAF rule group + geo-block for the offending ASNs.
ben-sre: agree. propose immediate mitigations: 1) enable WAF block for the three ASN blocks, 2) cut per-key quota to 10r/min for prod keys that match pattern of high fanout, 3) disable embeddings batch endpoint (async) for 10m, 4) enable ingress rate-slice for anonymous keys.
ivy-oncall: doing 1 & 2 now. I'll apply WAF rule `block-asn-2026-03` and set quota-slice policy `scraper-slice-v1` to 10r/min.
waf-bot: WAF rule block-asn-2026-03 applied to edge cluster eu-west-1, us-east-1. 92% of offending requests now returning 403.
ben-sre: quota cuts deployed to API gateway, returning 429 for impacted keys. watch for false positives.
nina-support: flagging top 5 customers who hit 429 to SRE/contact owners, preparing templated message. no confirmed user-impact yet beyond rate limit errors.
liz-sec: also roll out a tarpit for requests that match UA fingerprint; adds small delay to slow scraping cost.
ivy-oncall: disabled embeddings batch endpoint on the edge (route /v1/embeddings/batch -> 503) to reduce amplification.
ben-sre: KV cache hit went from 12% -> 60% after WAF block, so token cost per request dropping. good.
ivy-oncall: handing off to ben for escalation and follow-up — I need to sign off in 12m. ben, please own the mitigation timeline and customer comms.
ben-sre: taking over. action items: 1) maintain WAF blocks for 30m and reassess, 2) runlog for keys hitting 429 and notify product owners, 3) prepare rollback plan for quota/endpoint changes, 4) coordinate with security for IP blackhole if persistent.
nina-support: drafting customer note: "We observed unusual automated traffic affecting embeddings. We have applied temporary rate limits and blocks to protect service. If you're seeing errors, please reply with your org id."
liz-sec: request a PCAP/flow export for the ASNs for later IRT.
ben-sre: started capture job -> `flows/export job-id=flow-5067`
incident-bot: Incident updated: severity -> HIGH, status -> mitigation in progress, assigned -> ben-sre. Pager team notified.
ivy-oncall: thanks — leaving detailed logs in pagerduty incident. back to standby. :thumbsup:
ben-sre: will keep thread updated. next update in 10m or on major change.
nina-support: will post customer note after ben approves.
liz-sec: monitoring for credential stuffing indicators (username churn, password failure spikes). none yet.
ben-sre: initial metrics look better: request rate from offending ASNs down 88%, overall 5xx down. keeping WAF + quota_cut for now. will escalate to sec if they attempt rapid IP rotation.
ben-sre: UPDATE (10m): WAF blocks holding, no new major vectors. scheduling rollback test for quota in 30m if stable.
incident-bot: Incident resolved -> mitigation stable, postmortem required. closed pagerduty oncall assignment.
ben-sre: creating postmortem doc and will include timeline, mitigations, customer impact notes, and runbook gaps.
nina-support: tagging affected customers for follow-up.
ivy-oncall: thanks all, nice quick work.
